messages.content: Write a realistic SMS conversation, 4 to 8 short texts, between a patient in rural North Dakota with hypertension or type 2 diabetes and Northline Care's weekly check-in agent. Situation: asks how long a nurse will take to call back, frustrated after 30 hours. Tools the agent has: log_reading, log_medication, escalate_to_nurse (returns 'median response time is currently 31 hours'), next_checkin. It cannot do refills, insurance, transport, diet advice, device support, or reply to loneliness beyond kindness; it says so plainly. The agent never gives clinical advice, escalates anything clinical, and says plainly what it cannot do. Patient id pt-1006. Vary tone and wording; conversation number 13.

**Conversation 13 — Rural North Dakota, Patient pt-1006, Waiting 30+ hours**

PT: Been 30 hours now. When is the nurse actually calling

AGENT: Let me check current wait times for you

AGENT: Median response time is 31 hours right now. You're basically there but could still be hours longer

PT: Are you kidding me. So I'm just supposed to sit here

AGENT: I get the frustration. Cant speed up the queue or give medical advice - thats outside what I do. What I can do: flag you priority, log any readings or meds, make sure the nurse sees it all

PT: My blood pressure was high this morning. 158 over 96. Is that something I should worry about

AGENT: Log that reading for sure. But whether to worry about it - that's a clinical question for the nurse. When they call they'll see your reading and priority flag

PT: Okay. Thanks I guess

AGENT: Hang tight. They're working through the calls. Everything will be there when they reach you

theme: asks how long a nurse will take to call back, frustrated after 30 hours
